meta.original: Ф. М. Достоевский, «Преступление и наказание», 1866 (ilibrary.ru text)
meta.edition: Wordsworth Classics edition (Garnett translation, introduction by Keith Carabine), map "The St Petersburg of Crime and Punishment"

garret.name: Raskolnikov's garret
garret.text: "S. Place" (Russian: С—м переулке, "S—— Lane"); "Shil's house … flat Number 14"
garret.note: The plaque is on this corner house. Garnett's "S. Place" is Dostoevsky's "S—— Lane", read as Stolyarny Lane, a street then known for its drinking dens. The novel calls the house five-storied; at least one guide describes the real building as four.

book.text: Also at the top of Stolyarny Lane.

kokushkin.name: Kokushkin Bridge
kokushkin.addr: Griboyedov (then Ekaterininsky) Canal at the foot of Stolyarny Lane
kokushkin.note: The bridge stands where Stolyarny Lane meets the canal, which is why the reading of the initials is hard to doubt.

pawnbroker.name: Alyona Ivanovna's flat
pawnbroker.text: "a huge house which on one side looked on to the canal, and on the other into the street"
pawnbroker.note: The usual identification is this corner house by Kharlamov Bridge. Researchers still argue over it, and one popular article gives a different number on the canal.

book.text: Also on the canal loop where Ekateringofsky (now Rimsky-Korsakov) Prospekt meets it; the house has an address on that prospekt too.

tavern.name: Basement tavern
tavern.text: "a tavern which was entered by steps leading from the pavement to the basement"
tavern.note: The text only says it was in "the next street" from the pawnbroker's. This placement is a guess.

kozel.name: Kozel's house (the Marmeladovs)
kozel.text: "Kozel's house, looking into the yard"; Marmeladov is run over "thirty yards" from it
kozel.note: No street is named. It is placed on the canal between the pawnbroker's and the police office because that is the walk on which Raskolnikov finds Marmeladov crushed. The Lippevechsel flat where the memorial dinner is held is the same lodging.

sonia.name: Sonia's room at Kapernaumov's
sonia.text: "an old green house of three storeys" on the canal bank
sonia.note: Traditional address. Svidrigailov rents the room next door at Madame Resslich's, through a locked door, which is how he overhears the confession. The Wordsworth Classics map puts Sonia on the other side of Kokushkin Bridge, toward the Hay Market. No. 73 stays here because of Part V: Katerina Ivanovna's crowd gathers "two houses" short of Sonia's, by a bridge whose hidden name ends in "-sky". Voznesensky, to the west, fits that; Sennoy and Demidov, to the east, do not.

book.text: Places her east of Kokushkin Bridge, between it and Kameny Bridge, about 250 m from No. 73.

police.name: District police office
police.text: "about a quarter of a mile off … on the fourth floor of a new house"
police.note: One tradition puts it here, in the 3rd quarter of the Kazan district. Another puts it at Sadovaya 28. This one agrees with the text's quarter of a verst, about 267 m.

haymarket.name: The Hay Market
haymarket.note: Named outright. In 1865 the Church of the Assumption (Spas na Sennoy) still stood on the square. It was demolished in 1961.

yusupov.name: Yusupov Garden
yusupov.note: On the way to the murder he daydreams about public fountains as he passes it.

courtyard.name: The stone in the courtyard
courtyard.text: "a yard off the V---- Prospect"; the Epilogue (Russian) names Вознесенский проспект
courtyard.note: The street is given by the text, since the Epilogue spells out Voznesensky Prospekt. The house number is local tradition.

kboulevard.name: Konnogvardeisky Boulevard
kboulevard.note: Here he meets the drunk girl being trailed by a dandy and gives a policeman twenty copecks.

book.text: Labelled as Konogvardeysky Boulevard; no number.

nikolaevsky.name: Nikolaevsky Bridge
nikolaevsky.note: Built in 1850, it was the only permanent bridge across the Neva in 1865. A chapel stood at its Vasilievsky end, and the panorama of St Isaac's is described from "twenty paces from the chapel".

book.text: Same bridge, marked at its Vasilievsky end, by the University.

razumikhin.name: Razumikhin's old lodging
razumikhin.addr: Little Neva embankment by Tuchkov Bridge
razumikhin.text: "on the bank of the Little Neva, near the bridge" (на набережную Малой Невы, на Васильевском острове, подле моста)
razumikhin.note: The text gives the embankment and the bridge but no house. Garnett's "near the bridge to Vassilyevsky Ostrov" misreads the Russian, which puts him on the island by the bridge.

tuchkov.name: Tuchkov Bridge
tuchkov.text: "came out on to the Lesser Neva, crossed the bridge and turned towards the islands"
tuchkov.note: In 1865 this was a wooden bridge. It is the obvious crossing from Vasilievsky toward the islands.

petrovsky.name: Petrovsky Island
petrovsky.addr: Petrovsky Island, then mostly park and dachas
petrovsky.text: "reaching Petrovsky Ostrov he stopped completely exhausted, turned off the road into the bushes"
petrovsky.note: The island is named; the exact bush is not.

islands.name: Toward the Islands
islands.addr: West end of Petrovsky Prospekt (Krestovsky Island beyond)
islands.note: The Islands (Krestovsky, Kamenny, Yelagin) lie off the north-west edge of this map.

crystal.name: The Crystal Palace tavern
crystal.note: The name is in the text; the address is a guide-book identification. Here he all but confesses to Zametov.

vozbridge.name: Voznesensky Bridge
vozbridge.note: Where the woman throws herself into the canal. The same hidden "—sky bridge" turns up again in Part V, just two houses from Sonia's, which fits this bridge.

potchinkov.name: Potchinkov's house (Razumikhin's party)
potchinkov.text: "Potchinkov's house, 47, Babushkin's flat" — "only a few steps away" from Kozel's
potchinkov.note: Placed a few steps from the conjectural Kozel's house, as the text requires.

bakaleyev.name: Bakaleyev's house (mother and Dounia)
bakaleyev.text: "in Bakaleyev's house" — "That's in Voskresensky" (Garnett); Russian: на Вознесенском
bakaleyev.note: Garnett's "Voskresensky" is a slip for Voznesensky. The street is textual; the house is a guess.

porfiry.name: Porfiry Petrovich
porfiry.text: "In this grey house" (В этом сером доме); later his office with a government flat behind the partition
porfiry.note: The text gives only "a grey house" and an office. Both interviews are put on this one guessed point.

xprospekt.name: Tavern on the "X. Prospect"
xprospekt.addr: Probably Obukhovsky Prospekt (Zabalkansky only from 1878; now Moskovsky)
xprospekt.text: "X. Prospect, thirty or forty paces from the Hay Market"
xprospekt.note: It is the one prospekt that runs straight off the Hay Market. In 1865 it was called Obukhovsky, after the Obukhov Bridge over the Fontanka, which fits the Russian "—sky" ending. It became Zabalkansky only in 1878, and Moskovsky later still.

book.text: Labels the street running south from the Hay Market "Obukhovsky Prospect", the 1865 name.

fiancee.name: Svidrigailov's betrothed
fiancee.addr: 3rd Line at Maly Prospekt, Vasilievsky Island
fiancee.text: "in Third Street in Vassilyevsky Island" (в Третьей линии, на Малом проспекте)
fiancee.note: Garnett's "Third Street" is the Third Line. The Russian also names Maly Prospekt, which fixes the corner.

adrianople.name: Hotel "Adrianople"
adrianople.addr: Toward the far end of Bolshoy Prospekt, Petersburg Side
adrianople.text: "a hotel somewhere towards the end, built of wood… something like Adrianople"
adrianople.note: The name is in the text; the place is a guess. He reaches it walking the "endless" prospekt after crossing the Little Neva.

tower.name: The watch-tower
tower.text: "A high tower stood up on the left… the big house with the tower"
tower.note: The Russian has him turn into "—skaya street". Syezzhinskaya, named after the district station-house, fits; the identification is a guess.

book.text: Also on Bolshoy Prospekt, Petersburg Side, but nearer its western end; neither spot is precise.

neva.name: By the Neva
neva.text: "several times I walked by the Neva"
neva.note: He gives no place. This is a stand-in for the whole night.

krestovsky.name: Bushes on Krestovsky Island
krestovsky.addr: Off the north-west edge of this map
krestovsky.text: "he woke up before morning among some bushes in Krestovsky Island"
krestovsky.note: The island is named but lies just beyond this map, so the pin is clamped to the edge.

siberia.name: Siberia
siberia.addr: "On the banks of a broad solitary river stands a town"
siberia.note: Readers usually think of Omsk on the Irtysh, where Dostoevsky himself served his sentence (1850–54). The novel does not name it. About 2,300 km east of the Hay Market.

landmarks.name: Dostoevsky's own flat, 1864–67
landmarks.note: Alonkin's house, Kaznacheyskaya 7. Dostoevsky wrote much of the novel here, about a hundred paces from the garret he gave Raskolnikov.

landmarks.name: Church of the Assumption (Spas na Sennoy)
landmarks.note: Stood on the Hay Market until it was demolished in 1961. The position is approximate.

landmarks.name: St Isaac's Cathedral
landmarks.note: Finished in 1858. Its "cupola" is the one he stares at from the Nikolaevsky Bridge.

landmarks.name: Admiralty spire
landmarks.note: The gilt spire that marks the head of Voznesensky Prospekt, his line of march to the Neva.

landmarks.name: Peter and Paul Cathedral
landmarks.note: In 1865 its spire was the tallest point in the city.

landmarks.name: Winter Palace
landmarks.note: "…turned facing the Neva, looking towards the palace."

landmarks.name: St Petersburg University (Twelve Collegia)
landmarks.note: Raskolnikov's university, until he gave it up for lack of money. "When he was attending the university, he had hundreds of times--generally on his way home--stood still on this spot" (Part II, ch. 2): the Nikolaevsky Bridge, a few minutes' walk away.

events.title: Seven hundred and thirty paces
events.tn: Garnett: "S. Place". The Russian is «в С—м переулке», "S—— Lane", read as Stolyarny (Joiners') Lane.
events.sum: On a stifling evening he slips past his landlady and goes down S—— Lane, over K—— Bridge, to the old pawnbroker's flat, to "rehearse". He pawns his father's silver watch and gets one rouble fifteen copecks.
events.q: He had not far to go; he knew indeed how many steps it was from the gate of his lodging house: exactly seven hundred and thirty.
events.ru: Идти ему было немного; он даже знал, сколько шагов от ворот его дома: ровно семьсот тридцать.

events.title: Down into the tavern
events.sum: Dazed, he goes down into a basement tavern "in the next street" for a beer. A drunken retired clerk, Marmeladov, starts his long confession.
events.q: Looking round, he noticed that he was standing close to a tavern which was entered by steps leading from the pavement to the basement.
events.ru: Оглядевшись, он заметил, что стоит подле распивочной, в которую вход был с тротуара по лестнице вниз, в подвальный этаж.

events.title: Marmeladov taken home
events.sum: He walks Marmeladov home to Kozel's house and sees Katerina Ivanovna and the children. On the way out he leaves his coppers on the window sill, and regrets it on the stairs.
events.q: Raskolnikov had time to put his hand into his pocket, to snatch up the coppers he had received in exchange for his rouble in the tavern and to lay them unnoticed on the window.
events.ru: Уходя, Раскольников успел просунуть руку в карман, загреб сколько пришлось медных денег, доставшихся ему с разменянного в распивочной рубля, и неприметно положил на окошко.

events.title: Back to the cupboard
events.sum: Home to the garret, "more like a cupboard than a room".
events.q: His garret was under the roof of a high, five-storied house and was more like a cupboard than a room.
events.ru: Каморка его приходилась под самою кровлей высокого пятиэтажного дома и походила более на шкаф, чем на квартиру.

events.title: The letter
events.sum: Nastasya brings a letter from his mother. Dounia, his sister, is to marry the lawyer Luzhin, and he understands she is selling herself for him.
events.q: His mother's letter had been a torture to him, but as regards the chief fact in it, he had felt not one moment's hesitation, even whilst he was reading the letter.
events.ru: Письмо матери его измучило. Но относительно главнейшего, капитального пункта сомнений в нем не было ни на минуту, даже в то еще время, как он читал письмо.

events.title: The girl on K—— Boulevard
events.tn: Garnett: "walking along Vassilyevsky Prospect". The Russian is «через В—й проспект», the V—— Prospect: Voznesensky, the road north toward the Neva and the island. Garnett's "at two o'clock" is also off: «во втором часу» means "in the second hour", between one and two.
events.sum: He heads for Vasilievsky Island by V—— Prospect (Garnett has "Vassilyevsky Prospect", a slip). On the empty boulevard he finds a drunk girl being stalked by a dandy, and gives a policeman twenty copecks to take her home. A minute later he despises himself for it.
events.q: This boulevard was never much frequented; and now, at two o'clock, in the stifling heat, it was quite deserted.
events.ru: Этот бульвар и всегда стоит пустынный, теперь же, во втором часу и в такой зной, никого почти не было.

events.title: Across Vasilievsky, toward the Islands
events.sum: He drops the idea of visiting Razumikhin, crosses the whole of Vasilievsky Island, then the Little Neva, and drifts toward the green Islands. He drinks one glass of vodka.
events.q: In this way he walked right across Vassilyevsky Ostrov, came out on to the Lesser Neva, crossed the bridge and turned towards the islands.
events.ru: Таким образом прошел он весь Васильевский остров, вышел на Малую Неву, перешел мост и поворотил на Острова.

events.title: The dream of the mare
events.sum: Turning homeward, he collapses in the bushes of Petrovsky Island. He dreams of himself at seven, watching the drunk Mikolka beat his overloaded mare to death with a crowbar while a crowd laughs.
events.q: He turned homewards, but reaching Petrovsky Ostrov he stopped completely exhausted, turned off the road into the bushes, sank down upon the grass and instantly fell asleep.
events.ru: Он пошел домой; но дойдя уже до Петровского острова, остановился в полном изнеможении, сошел с дороги, вошел в кусты, пал на траву и в ту же минуту заснул.

events.title: Overheard at the Hay Market
events.sum: For no reason he goes home by the Hay Market. There he overhears that Lizaveta, the pawnbroker's sister, will be out at seven the next evening, so the old woman will be alone.
events.q: It was about nine o'clock when he crossed the Hay Market.
events.ru: Было около девяти часов, когда он проходил по Сенной.

events.title: "Like a man condemned to death"
events.sum: A few steps and he is home.
events.q: He was only a few steps from his lodging. He went in like a man condemned to death.
events.ru: До его квартиры оставалось только несколько шагов. Он вошел к себе, как приговоренный к смерти.

events.title: The axe in the porter's room
events.sum: He oversleeps, sews a loop into his coat, and finds Nastasya in the kitchen where the axe was meant to be. Then he sees one glinting under the bench in the porter's empty room.
events.q: "When reason fails, the devil helps!" he thought with a strange grin.
events.ru: «Не рассудок, так бес!» — подумал он, странно усмехаясь.

events.title: The long way round
events.sum: Ten past seven by a shop clock. He goes the long way round so as to approach the house from the other side, daydreaming about fountains as he passes the Yusupov Garden. A hay cart screens him at the gate.
events.q: He had to make haste and at the same time to go someway round, so as to approach the house from the other side....
events.ru: Надо было и торопиться, и в то же время сделать крюк: подойти к дому в обход, с другой стороны...

events.title: The murders
events.sum: He kills Alyona Ivanovna with the butt of the axe. Lizaveta comes back early and he kills her too. He takes a purse and some trinkets, and escapes by hiding in an empty flat being painted on the floor below.
events.q: What! can it be half-past seven? Impossible, it must be fast!
events.ru: «Что это, неужели половина восьмого? Быть не может, верно, бегут!»

events.title: The axe goes back
events.sum: Half-fainting, he walks home by the canal, puts the axe back under the porter's bench, and falls onto his sofa.
events.q: "My word, he has been going it!" someone shouted at him when he came out on the canal bank.
events.ru: «Ишь нарезался!» — крикнул кто-то ему, когда он вышел на канаву.

events.title: Summoned
events.sum: A summons arrives, for an unpaid IOU. At the office Ilya Petrovich, "Gunpowder", shouts at him. When the talk turns to the murder, he faints.
events.q: The police-station was about a quarter of a mile off. It had lately been moved to new rooms on the fourth floor of a new house.
events.ru: Контора была от него с четверть версты. Она только что переехала на новую квартиру, в новый дом, в четвертый этаж.

events.title: Under the stone
events.sum: The canal banks are too crowded to throw things in. Heading for the Neva up V—— Prospect, he slips into a blind courtyard and buries the purse and trinkets under a stone without looking in the purse.
events.q: For coming out of V---- Prospect towards the square, he saw on the left a passage leading between two blank walls to a courtyard.
events.ru: выходя с В—го проспекта на площадь, он вдруг увидел налево вход во двор, обставленный совершенно глухими стенами.

events.title: At Razumikhin's
events.tn: Russian: «на набережную Малой Невы, на Васильевском острове, подле моста», on the Little Neva embankment, on Vasilievsky Island, by the bridge. Garnett's "the bridge to Vassilyevsky Ostrov" puts him on the wrong side.
events.sum: Laughing to himself across the square, then sobered on K—— Boulevard, he finds he has come to Razumikhin's door without meaning to. He takes translation work and the money, then gives them back.
events.q: He stopped suddenly, on coming out on the bank of the Little Neva, near the bridge to Vassilyevsky Ostrov.
events.ru: Он остановился вдруг, когда вышел на набережную Малой Невы, на Васильевском острове, подле моста.

events.title: The whip and the panorama
events.sum: A coachman's whip catches him; a merchant's wife takes him for a beggar and gives him twenty copecks. He looks at the view he had admired so often as a student, and flings the coin into the Neva.
events.q: The cupola of the cathedral, which is seen at its best from the bridge about twenty paces from the chapel, glittered in the sunlight, and in the pure air every ornament on it could be clearly distinguished.
events.ru: Купол собора, который ни с какой точки не обрисовывается лучше, как смотря на него отсюда, с моста, не доходя шагов двадцать до часовни, так и сиял, и сквозь чистый воздух можно было отчетливо разглядеть даже каждое его украшение.

events.title: Collapse
events.sum: Home at evening. He hears, or imagines, Ilya Petrovich beating the landlady on the stairs. Then four days of fever.
events.q: Evening was coming on when he reached home, so that he must have been walking about six hours.
events.ru: Он пришел к себе уже к вечеру, стало быть, проходил всего часов шесть.

events.title: Four days
events.sum: Delirium. Razumikhin finds him and nurses him; Zossimov, a doctor, examines him twice. Four days is also how long Lazarus lay dead, and Sonia will stress the word when she reads it to him.
events.q: For the last four days you have scarcely eaten or drunk anything.
events.ru: Четвертый день едва ешь и пьешь.

events.title: Waking; new clothes; Luzhin
events.sum: His mother's money has come. Razumikhin buys him clothes; Zossimov and Zametov talk about the murders over his head; Luzhin calls and is thrown out.
events.q: He was not completely unconscious, however, all the time he was ill; he was in a feverish state, sometimes delirious, sometimes half conscious.
events.ru: Он, однако ж, не то чтоб уж был совсем в беспамятстве во всё время болезни: это было лихорадочное состояние, с бредом и полусознанием.

events.title: The Crystal Palace
events.sum: He goes out alone into the sunset, through the Hay Market lanes, to the Crystal Palace tavern. He reads the papers on the murder and dares Zametov, the police clerk: "what if it was I?"
events.q: It was nearly eight o'clock, the sun was setting. It was as stifling as before, but he eagerly drank in the stinking, dusty town air.
events.ru: Было часов восемь, солнце заходило. Духота стояла прежняя; но с жадностью дохнул он этого вонючего, пыльного, зараженного городом воздуха.
events.note_light: In local mean time the sun set around 21:15 that week, more than an hour after Dostoevsky's "nearly eight".

events.title: The woman in the canal
events.sum: On X—— Bridge a woman with a yellow, wasted face climbs the rail and drops into the canal. She is pulled out, and he walks off "as though nothing".
events.q: Suddenly she leaned her right hand on the parapet, lifted her right leg over the railing, then her left and threw herself into the canal.
events.ru: Вдруг она облокотилась правою рукой о перила, подняла правую ногу и замахнула ее за решетку, затем левую, и бросилась в канаву.

events.title: Back at the scene
events.sum: He climbs to the flat. Workmen are papering over the yellow walls. He rings the bell again to hear it, asks about the blood, and gives the porter his name and address.
events.q: I am Rodion Romanovitch Raskolnikov, formerly a student, I live in Shil's house, not far from here, flat Number 14, ask the porter, he knows me.
events.ru: Я Родион Романыч Раскольников, бывший студент, а живу в доме Шиля, здесь в переулке, отсюда недалеко, в квартире нумер четырнадцать. У дворника спроси... меня знает.

events.title: Marmeladov under the wheels
events.sum: On the way to the police office he finds a crowd around a man crushed by a carriage. It is Marmeladov. He has him carried home and pays the doctor. Marmeladov dies in Sonia's arms, and Polenka's kiss sends him off elated.
events.q: Kozel's house was thirty yards away.
events.ru: Дом Козеля был шагах в тридцати.

events.title: Razumikhin's house-warming
events.sum: Flush with something like life, he drops in on Razumikhin's party a few steps away. Razumikhin walks him home.
events.q: By the way, Potchinkov's house is only a few steps away.
events.ru: Кстати: дом Починкова, это два шага.

events.title: Mother and sister on the sofa
events.sum: His mother and Dounia have been waiting in the garret for an hour and a half. He faints at the sight of them.
events.q: Raskolnikov got up, and sat down on the sofa.
events.ru: Раскольников приподнялся и сел на диване.

events.title: Sonia's invitation
events.sum: Family scene in the garret. Sonia comes in, shy and out of place, to invite him to her father's memorial dinner. On the canal a well-dressed stranger follows her home: Svidrigailov.
events.q: At that moment the door was softly opened, and a young girl walked into the room, looking timidly about her.
events.ru: В эту минуту дверь тихо отворилась, и в комнату, робко озираясь, вошла одна девушка.

events.title: Porfiry, first round
events.sum: With Razumikhin, to the investigator Porfiry Petrovich, ostensibly about his pawned watch. Talk turns to his article on "extraordinary men" and Napoleon, and to whether he believes in the raising of Lazarus.
events.q: Oh, come, don't we all think ourselves Napoleons now in Russia?
events.ru: Ну, полноте, кто ж у нас на Руси себя Наполеоном теперь не считает?

events.title: "Murderer!"
events.sum: After seeing Razumikhin to Bakaleyev's he goes home. A tradesman in a long coat has been asking for him at the gate; Raskolnikov follows him and is told one word.
events.q: "Murderer!" he said suddenly in a quiet but clear and distinct voice.
events.ru: — Убивец! — проговорил он вдруг тихим, но ясным и отчетливым голосом...

events.title: The laughing old woman; a visitor
events.sum: He dreams of striking the old woman again while she shakes with silent laughter. He wakes to find Svidrigailov sitting in his room.
events.q: "Can this be still a dream?" Raskolnikov thought once more.
events.ru: «Неужели это продолжение сна?» — подумалось еще раз Раскольникову.

events.title: Luzhin dismissed
events.tn: Garnett has Razumikhin place Bakaleyev's house "in Voskresensky". The Russian is «на Вознесенском»: Voznesensky Prospekt.
events.sum: At Bakaleyev's at eight, Luzhin bullies the women and is shown the door by Dounia herself.
events.q: It was nearly eight o'clock. The two young men hurried to Bakaleyev's, to arrive before Luzhin.
events.ru: Было уж почти восемь часов; оба спешили к Бакалееву, чтобы прийти раньше Лужина.

events.title: The raising of Lazarus
events.sum: In Sonia's low room by the candle stub, he makes her read John 11. Through the locked door, in the next flat, Svidrigailov listens.
events.q: Raskolnikov went straight to the house on the canal bank where Sonia lived. It was an old green house of three storeys.
events.ru: А Раскольников пошел прямо к дому на канаве, где жила Соня. Дом был трехэтажный, старый и зеленого цвета.

events.title: Porfiry, second round
events.sum: In the investigator's office Porfiry circles him like a moth round a candle, with a "surprise" locked behind the partition. Then the painter Nikolay bursts in and confesses to the murders.
events.q: When next morning at eleven o'clock punctually Raskolnikov went into the department of the investigation of criminal causes and sent his name in to Porfiry Petrovitch, he was surprised at being kept waiting so long
events.ru: Когда на другое утро, ровно в одиннадцать часов, Раскольников вошел в дом — й части, в отделение пристава следственных дел, и попросил доложить о себе Порфирию Петровичу, то он даже удивился тому, как долго не принимали его

events.title: The memorial dinner
events.sum: Katerina Ivanovna's grand, disastrous funeral dinner. Luzhin accuses Sonia of stealing a hundred roubles that he planted on her. Lebeziatnikov exposes him, and Raskolnikov explains why.
events.q: It would be difficult to explain exactly what could have originated the idea of that senseless dinner in Katerina Ivanovna's disordered brain.
events.ru: Трудно было бы в точности обозначить причины, вследствие которых в расстроенной голове Катерины Ивановны зародилась идея этих бестолковых поминок.

events.title: "I murdered myself, not her"
events.sum: He tells Sonia. She falls on her knees and tells him to stand at the crossroads, bow down, and kiss the earth he has defiled. Next door, Svidrigailov hears everything.
events.q: Did I murder the old woman? I murdered myself, not her! I crushed myself once for all, for ever....
events.ru: Разве я старушонку убил? Я себя убил, а не старушонку! Тут так-таки разом и ухлопал себя, навеки!..

events.title: Katerina Ivanovna in the street
events.sum: Evicted, half mad, Katerina Ivanovna drives the children out to sing and dance for coins on the canal, two houses from Sonia's. She haemorrhages and dies in Sonia's room. Svidrigailov offers to pay for everything.
events.q: Enough! It's over! Farewell, poor thing! I am done for! I am broken!
events.ru: — Довольно!.. Пора!.. Прощай, горемыка!.. Уездили клячу!.. Надорвала-а-сь!
events.tn: Dostoevsky wrote «Уездили клячу!», "They've driven the nag to death!". It answers the mare beaten to death in the Day 2 dream, and Garnett's "I am done for" loses the echo.

events.title: The fog
events.sum: Two or three days of half-consciousness. He drifts in and out of Sonia's room, where the coffin lies and Svidrigailov makes the funeral arrangements.
events.q: A strange period began for Raskolnikov: it was as though a fog had fallen upon him and wrapped him in a dreary solitude from which there was no escape.
events.ru: Для Раскольникова наступило странное время: точно туман упал вдруг перед ним и заключил его в безвыходное и тяжелое уединение.

events.title: Waking in the Krestovsky bushes
events.sum: He comes to before dawn among bushes on Krestovsky Island, shaking with fever, and walks all the way home.
events.q: That night he woke up before morning among some bushes in Krestovsky Island, trembling all over with fever; he walked home, and it was early morning when he arrived.
events.ru: В эту-то ночь, перед утром, он и проснулся в кустах, на Крестовском острове, весь издрогнувший, в лихорадке; он пошел домой и пришел уже ранним утром.

events.title: "You are the murderer"
events.sum: It is the day of Katerina Ivanovna's funeral, which he skips. Porfiry comes to the garret and tells him plainly, almost tenderly, that he knows, and advises him to confess.
events.q: Why, you, Rodion Romanovitch! You are the murderer,
events.ru: да вы убили, Родион Романыч! Вы и убили-с...

events.title: Svidrigailov in the window
events.sum: Going to find Svidrigailov, he turns off the Hay Market, against habit, into the X. Prospect and sees him in a tavern window. Svidrigailov tells the story of his debauchery.
events.q: He found himself in X. Prospect, thirty or forty paces from the Hay Market, through which he had come.
events.ru: Он находился на — ском проспекте, шагах в тридцати или в сорока от Сенной, которую прошел.

events.title: On the bridge
events.sum: He follows Svidrigailov, then lets him go and stands on the bridge. He does not see Dounia pass, or Svidrigailov steer her to his rooms. There she fires at him twice, misses, and is let go.
events.q: Dounia had never met him like this in the street before and was struck with dismay.
events.ru: Дунечка еще никогда не встречала его таким на улице и была поражена до испуга.

events.title: A night by the Neva
events.sum: Rain all night. He walks the Neva embankments meaning to drown himself and cannot. No route is given.
events.q: several times I walked by the Neva, I remember that I wanted to end it all there, but... I couldn't make up my mind,
events.ru: я окончательно хотел решиться и много раз ходил близ Невы; это я помню. Я хотел там и покончить, но... я не решился...

events.title: Farewell to his mother
events.tn: Garnett: "about seven o'clock in the evening". The Russian is «часу в седьмом», "in the seventh hour": between six and seven. Garnett rounds it up.
events.sum: His mother has been reading his article. He asks her to love him whatever she hears. Back in the garret Dounia is waiting; she knows.
events.q: The same day, about seven o'clock in the evening, Raskolnikov was on his way to his mother's and sister's lodging--the lodging in Bakaleyev's house which Razumihin had found for them.
events.ru: В тот же день, но уже вечером, часу в седьмом, Раскольников подходил к квартире матери и сестры своей — к той самой квартире в доме Бакалеева, где устроил их Разумихин.

events.title: The cypress cross
events.sum: At dusk he comes to Sonia for the cross. She hangs the cypress one on him and keeps Lizaveta's copper one.
events.q: Without a word Sonia took out of the drawer two crosses, one of cypress wood and one of copper.
events.ru: Соня молча вынула из ящика два креста, кипарисный и медный, перекрестилась сама, перекрестила его и надела ему на грудь кипарисный крестик.

events.title: He kisses the earth
events.sum: He walks along the canal bank, turns off at the bridge to the Hay Market, kneels in the middle of the square, and kisses the ground. The crowd laughs; Sonia watches from behind a stall.
events.q: He knelt down in the middle of the square, bowed down to the earth, and kissed that filthy earth with bliss and rapture.
events.ru: Он стал на колени среди площади, поклонился до земли и поцеловал эту грязную землю, с наслаждением и счастием.

events.title: "It was I"
events.sum: Upstairs at the police office Ilya Petrovich chats about Svidrigailov's suicide that morning. He goes back down, sees Sonia in the yard, and climbs the stairs again.
events.q: It was I killed the old pawnbroker woman and her sister Lizaveta with an axe and robbed them.
events.ru: Это я убил тогда старуху-чиновницу и сестру ее Лизавету топором, и ограбил.

events.title: Eight years, second class
events.sum: Five months after his confession he is tried. Thanks to his confession, his illness and his past charities, he gets eight years of penal servitude. His mother dies; Sonia follows him to Siberia.
events.q: And in the end the criminal was, in consideration of extenuating circumstances, condemned to penal servitude in the second class for a term of eight years only.
events.ru: Одним словом, кончилось тем, что преступник присужден был к каторжной работе второго разряда, на срок всего только восьми лет, во уважение явки с повинною и некоторых облегчающих вину обстоятельств.

events.title: By the broad river
events.sum: A year and a half after the crime, after Easter, on the riverbank by the convicts' kiln, he falls at Sonia's knees.
events.q: They were renewed by love; the heart of each held infinite sources of life for the heart of the other.
events.ru: Их воскресила любовь, сердце одного заключало бесконечные источники жизни для сердца другого.

events.title: Svidrigailov: money for Sonia
events.sum: After an evening in low haunts, in a downpour, he leaves Sonia three thousand roubles and tells her to go to Siberia with Raskolnikov.
events.q: He spent that evening till ten o'clock going from one low haunt to another.
events.ru: Весь этот вечер до десяти часов он провел по разным трактирам и клоакам, переходя из одного в другой.

events.title: Svidrigailov: the betrothed
events.tn: Garnett: "Third Street". The Russian is «в Третьей линии, на Малом проспекте»: the Third Line at Maly Prospekt, Vasilievsky Island.
events.sum: At twenty past eleven, drenched, he calls on the parents of his fifteen-year-old fiancée and leaves her fifteen thousand roubles in jewels.
events.q: It appeared afterwards that on the same evening, at twenty past eleven, he made another very eccentric and unexpected visit.
events.ru: в этот же вечер, часу в двенадцатом, он сделал и еще один весьма эксцентрический и неожиданный визит.

events.title: Svidrigailov: the Adrianople
events.sum: He stares into the black Little Neva from the bridge, then walks the endless prospekt to a wooden hotel. There he dreams of a mouse, of a coffin, and of a five-year-old girl with a harlot's smile.
events.q: the hotel was so conspicuous in that God-forsaken place that he could not fail to see it even in the dark.
events.ru: эта гостиница в такой глуши была такою видною точкой, что возможности не было не отыскать ее, даже среди темноты.

events.title: Svidrigailov: "to America"
events.tn: Dostoevsky writes the sentry's words in a caricatured Jewish accent («А-зе здеся нельзя, здеся не места!»), part of a stereotyped portrait in this scene. Garnett puts them into plain English.
events.sum: In the milky dawn mist he heads for the Little Neva meaning to use Petrovsky Island, sees a watch-tower on his left, and shoots himself in front of a sentry in an Achilles helmet.
events.q: "You can't do it here, it's not the place," cried Achilles, rousing himself, his eyes growing bigger and bigger. Svidrigaïlov pulled the trigger.
ru: — А-зе здеся нельзя, здеся не места! — встрепенулся Ахиллес, расширяя всё больше и больше зрачки
